title: Jam Session film (1944) and its recording personnel
summary: They go through the film's cast and the personnel for Barnet's Cherokee, noting that Killian, McGhee, Holland and Pettiford were replaced on camera.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Right. 1944, "Jam Session," 74 minutes, directed by Charles Barton. Poorly scripted and altogether uninspired musical, although rich in performers, featuring as it does Louis Armstrong and His Orchestra, with Lawrence Lucie Luthey, guitar, Charlie Barnet and His Band, Glenn Gray and

the Casa Loma Orchestra, the bands of Alvino Rey, Jan Garber, Teddy Powell, plus Jo Stafford, the Pied Pipers, and then it lists all the numbers. "St. Louis Blues," "No Name Jive," "Jive Bomber," recording personnel for "Cherokee," by Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra. Peanuts Holland, Al Killian, Howard McGhee, Paul Cohen, trumpets, Bob Swift, Eddie Burt, Trummy Young, Ed Fromm, trombones, Charlie Barnet, Steve Cole, George Savaro, alto sax.
Oh, that's why I couldn't -- it didn't look right. They have Savaro here.
Kurt Bloom, Mike Goldberg, tenor sax, Danny Bank, baritone sax, Ralph Burns, piano, Turk Van Lake, guitar, Chubby Jackson. Chubby Jackson and Oscar Pettiford, bass?
Yes. I had -- that's an interesting story, when we get around to it. I had both of them.
Lou Fromm, drums. Killian, McGhee, Holland and Pettiford do not appear on camera, as white actors sat in their places. Okay, tell me the bass story.
